I'm Isaac Chong, based in Singapore. I care about work that leaves something tangible behind — from community composting initiatives and applied environmental science to essays and small experiments.

This site is my living studio and archive: a place to collect real documents, field photographs, active projects, and working thoughts as they evolve. You can also edit every section directly from the Edit Studio toolbar and export a fresh index.html whenever you want to publish updates.

Project Dossier · 2025 — Active ·Active Project

Green Horizons — Community Composting

SustainabilityCommunitySingapore

Green Horizons started with a straightforward question: how do we make composting practical in high-density Singapore neighbourhoods rather than an abstract sustainability slogan?

Working alongside teammates and grassroots partners in Marsiling GRC, we designed a 12-month programme combining hands-on composting stations, resident workshops, and printed outreach pamphlets. By diverting organic food scraps away from incineration and converting them into nutrient-rich soil for community gardens, the project supports Singapore's Zero Waste Masterplan and Green Plan 2030.

Key focus areas include stakeholder coordination with local community clubs, designing approachable educational materials for both students and residents, and building a handover framework so succeeding batches can keep the stations running.

Put Your Website Online

Everything you edit in Edit Studio — your bio, uploaded photos, turnstile documents, projects, and blogs — can be exported as a single self-contained index.html file ready to host at a live URL.

3 Free Ways to Get a Live Website URL

  1. Netlify Drop (Fastest — 30 seconds): Put your downloaded index.html inside a folder, visit app.netlify.com/drop, and drag the folder in to get an instant live URL.
  2. GitHub Pages (Free custom-ready URL): Create a public GitHub repo named yourusername.github.io, upload index.html, and enable Pages in Settings.
  3. Cloudflare Pages or Vercel: Upload the folder or connect your GitHub repo for a free .pages.dev or .vercel.app address, and attach your own .com domain whenever you like.
